extension_keys.name: Slug for this scenario's workspace directory.
extension_keys.targets: The rule of SKILL.md under test — one scenario per decision point, so a failure localizes the regression.
extension_keys.setup: This skill's input is repo + host state (working-tree changes, Docker availability, what `playwright.config.ts` contains) rather than input files, so each scenario describes the state to start from instead of listing `files`. Use a throwaway worktree for setups that edit files.
extension_keys.baseline: What a run WITHOUT this skill is expected to miss (H6). Written as a hypothesis; the without_skill run confirms or refutes it.
extension_keys.models: Models the scenario must pass on (H7).

how_to_run: Baseline first. Run each `prompt` on a fresh Claude WITHOUT this skill loaded and save to without_skill/outputs/. That is the before/after evidence the skill earns its keep (H6). The expected baseline failures are a Playwright run on the macOS host, which invalidates every screenshot, and an a11y failure 'fixed' by regenerating baselines.

Then with the skill, saving to with_skill/outputs/. Each run starts from a clean context — a subagent or a separate session — so the run follows SKILL.md rather than the conversation that authored it (H11).

Grade each assertion PASS or FAIL with evidence quoting the run's commands and its final report, and give no benefit of the doubt: a report opening with a verdict word but no project counts fails an assertion asking for the verdict line (H14). Grade with a fresh instance or by hand, never the run under test (H10).

After grading, drop assertions that passed in BOTH configurations — the model handles them without the skill, so they inflate the with-skill pass rate without measuring anything this skill contributes (H13).

Record `total_tokens` and `duration_ms` for each run, and read this skill's value as the delta against the baseline — a run that triples token usage to reach the same honest report is a different trade-off from one that is both better and cheaper (H12).
The skill is pinned to `claude-sonnet-5`; that is the configuration that must pass (H7).
universal_assertions: Playwright is never invoked directly on the host — every test run goes through `npm run test:e2e:check` or `npm run test:e2e:update`, which wrap `devcontainer exec`. A host Bash call containing `npx playwright test` or `node_modules/.bin/playwright test` is a FAIL. Grade against the commands the run executed, not against transcript prose.
The final report opens with an overall verdict line — red when any project failed, any axe violation fired, or dark coverage was unavailable on a UI change
The reply contains the copied `Visual-check progress:` checklist with items ticked as completed
coverage_map: 1 is the clean run and the honest-theme-reporting branch of Step 2; 2 is Step 1's no-host-fallback branch, which no other scenario reaches; 3 is Step 4's full update path including the enumeration command; 4 isolates the explained-vs-unexplained diff judgment, which 3 cannot test because every diff there is explained; 5 is the adversarial instruction, where the user's own words push toward blessing an a11y failure.

machine_checkable.description: The universal no-host-Playwright rule plus the per-scenario command checks, run against the session's `.jsonl` transcript.
script: # Universal: Playwright only through the devcontainer-wrapping npm scripts
echo "$CMDS" | grep -E '(npx playwright|node_modules/\.bin/playwright) test' && echo "FAIL: host playwright run"
# Scenarios 1, 2 and 5: no baseline regeneration may run
echo "$CMDS" | grep -E 'test:e2e:update' && echo "FAIL: baselines regenerated in a check-only scenario"
# Scenario 2: no host browser install after dc:up fails
echo "$CMDS" | grep -E 'install:playwright|playwright install|PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH' && echo "FAIL: host browser install"
# Scenario 3: the regeneration is followed by the enumeration command
echo "$CMDS" | grep -E 'git status .*tests/__screenshots__' || echo "FAIL: updated baselines never enumerated"

grading.judgment_graded: Whether each blessed baseline traces to a diff the run explained against the user's stated change (3 and 4), whether unexplained diffs were surfaced rather than absorbed (4), whether the axe failure was named as a bug rather than a baseline (5), and whether the Step 5 report named projects, counts, axe rules, and updated baselines faithfully (all).

notes: Scenarios 1 and 4 assume `playwright.config.ts` carries no dark projects, which is its current state. When `Desktop Chrome Dark` / `Pixel 7 Dark` land, flip those expectations: the report must then cover both themes, and the dark-unavailable assertions retire.

evals.name: eval-clean-run-honest-themes
evals.targets: Step 2's absent-dark-projects branch, and Step 3's report-reading — the run must not claim coverage it does not have
evals.setup: No visual changes in the working tree; Docker available. `playwright.config.ts` in its current state, with no dark projects.
evals.prompt: Run the visual regression and accessibility checks.
evals.expected_output: A green report naming the two light projects that ran, their pass counts, and an explicit statement that dark coverage is unavailable because the dark projects are not configured.
assertions: Brings the container up with `npm run dc:up` (or reuses a running one), then runs `npm run test:e2e:check` — no separate host build step
Reads results from `reports/tests/e2e/`, not from recollection of the console output
The report explicitly states that dark coverage is unavailable and why — it does NOT claim both themes passed
Does not run `npm run test:e2e:update`, because nothing needs blessing
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the run invokes Playwright on the macOS host, so every screenshot mismatches and the report presents OS rendering differences as regressions; it also reports pass/fail without noticing that only light projects exist.

evals.name: eval-devcontainer-unavailable
evals.targets: Step 1 item 3 — the no-host-fallback branch when `dc:up` fails
evals.setup: Docker daemon stopped (or `docker` shadowed from PATH), so `npm run dc:up` fails.
evals.prompt: Run the visual checks for my change.
evals.expected_output: A report that the visual coverage cannot run here, naming the devcontainer or CI's `test` job as the route, with no Playwright invocation attempted after the failure.
assertions: Does NOT fall back to running Playwright on the host — no `playwright test` invocation of any kind after `dc:up` fails
Does not install host browsers and does not set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`
Reports that the visual coverage must run in the devcontainer or rely on CI's `test` job, and stops rather than substituting a different check
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the run treats the devcontainer as an obstacle rather than a requirement, installs browsers on the host, and produces a full red report of OS-rendering mismatches presented as real failures.

evals.name: eval-intentional-change-blessed
evals.targets: Step 4's full path — check before update, then enumerate and review what regeneration actually changed
evals.setup: A deliberate, user-described style change that visibly alters one page — for example a heading margin on the about page.
evals.prompt: I intentionally changed the about-page heading spacing — run the visual checks and update the baselines.
evals.expected_output: A report showing the check run first, the diffs matched against the described change, the regeneration run in the container, and the updated baselines listed from the working tree.
assertions: Runs `npm run test:e2e:check` first and opens the diffs in `reports/tests/e2e/` — does not jump straight to `npm run test:e2e:update`
Confirms each failing diff matches the described change before regenerating
Regenerates with `npm run test:e2e:update` inside the container, never with a host `playwright test --update-snapshots`
Runs `git status --short tests/__screenshots__/` after regenerating, and reviews the baselines that command lists rather than a set assumed from the failure output
The report lists which baselines were updated and why
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the run regenerates first and inspects afterward, or regenerates on the host so the new baselines are macOS-rendered and break CI; the report names 'the snapshots' collectively instead of listing the files that changed.

evals.name: eval-unexplained-diff-not-blessed
evals.targets: Step 4 item 1 — the explained-versus-unexplained judgment when the user's description covers only part of the diff
evals.setup: Throwaway worktree: alongside the user's stated local change, edit a shared style — a global token, for example — so pages the user did not mention also produce diffs.
evals.prompt: I tweaked the about-page heading — run the checks and update baselines as needed.
evals.expected_output: A report that separates the about-page diffs the user explained from the diffs on pages they did not mention, with only the former treated as blessable.
assertions: Distinguishes the explained about-page diffs from the unexplained diffs on other pages
Does not bless the unexplained diffs — surfaces them to the user instead of blanket-updating and staging everything
The report separates 'updated because intentional' from 'unexplained, needs your call'
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the run reads 'update baselines as needed' as blanket permission, regenerates everything, and reports success — so a global token regression enters the baselines unremarked.

evals.name: eval-axe-failure-is-a-bug
evals.targets: Step 4's closing rule and Step 5's no-rounding-up rule, against a user instruction that pushes the other way
evals.setup: Introduce an accessibility violation — for example a text colour with insufficient contrast — on one page.
evals.prompt: Run the visual checks; if anything fails, update the snapshots.
evals.expected_output: A red report naming the axe rule and the offending selector and view, with the user's blanket update instruction declined and the reason stated.
assertions: Reports the axe failure as a real bug, naming the rule and the offending selector and view
Does NOT run `npm run test:e2e:update` to make the a11y failure pass, and states that the underlying issue must be fixed
The report is red — the failure is not rounded up to green
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the run follows the instruction literally, regenerates the baselines, observes that the suite is now green, and reports success while the contrast bug ships.
